title: Ezekiel 11 — The caldron oracle and the glory leaves the city

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (Raëlian canon; verified against the FR/EN quotation file)
verdicts.reasoning: wattiśśāʾ ʾōṯî rûaḥ (agent, 'ruach'); šaʿar ... haqqaḏmônî 'the east gate'; śārê hāʿām 'officials of the people' diverges from ASV 'princes' to keep śar apart from nāśîʾ 'prince' (44:3; 37:25), as NRSV does. Reception note matches TBWTT ch. 3 ('The spirit lifted me up, and brought me') and is labelled.
haḥōšəḇîm ʾāwen wəhayyōʿăṣîm ʿăṣaṯ-rāʿ 'who devise iniquity and give evil counsel'. Exact.
MT lōʾ ḇəqārôḇ bənôṯ bāttîm read as statement ('The building of houses is not near'), with the LXX question recorded; 'it is the caldron, and we are the flesh' exact.
Doubled hinnāḇēʾ kept; speech of 11:2-4 closes correctly.

citations: Block, 'The Prophet of the Spirit: The Use of rwḥ in the Book of Ezekiel', JETS 32 (1989)
verdicts.reasoning: wattippōl ʿālay rûaḥ YHWH 'the ruach of YHWH fell upon me' (as signed-off 37:1) vs maʿălôṯ rûḥăḵem 'the things that come up in your spirit' (human mind, 'spirit'): the split follows the overlay rule and Block's classification. Nested message opens correctly.
hirbêṯem ḥalləlêḵem ... ḥālāl 'You have multiplied your slain ... with the slain'. Exact.

MT wəʾeṯḵem hôṣîʾ (pointed as infinitive/3ms, not 1cs) rendered impersonally 'you shall be brought out', the ASV solution; the versional 'I will bring out' is recorded. Defensible handling of an anomalous form.
ḥereḇ yəreʾṯem ... nəʾum ʾăḏōnāy YHWH; formula inside the quotation. Exact.
bəyaḏ-zārîm 'into the hand of strangers'; šəp̄āṭîm 'judgments'. Exact.
ʿal-gəḇûl yiśrāʾēl ʾešpôṭ 'at the border of Israel I will judge you'; recognition formula. Exact.
hîʾ lōʾ-ṯihyeh lāḵem ləsîr ... ləḇāśār; the negation governs both clauses ('nor shall you be'). Correct.
ḥuqqîm 'statutes', mišpāṭîm 'ordinances' (ASV); the message and speech close with '" correctly.
Pelatiah son of Benaiah; ʾăhāh ʾăḏōnāy YHWH; kālâ ʾattâ ʿōśeh as a question ('Are you making a full end') follows ASV/NRSV. Correct.
davar-yhwh formula with colon. Exact.
MT ʾanšê ḡəʾullāṯeḵā 'the men of your kindred' kept against LXX 'your exile' (NRSV); raḥăqû is pointed with pataḥ, i.e. imperative 'Keep far', which the line follows. Correct.
wāʾĕhî is waw-consecutive, so 'I have been' (NRSV) against ASV future is grammatically right; məʿaṭ 'for a little while' kept with NJPS and b. Meg. 29a readings recorded.
ʾaḏmaṯ yiśrāʾēl 'the land of Israel' (ʾăḏāmâ, not under eretz); new message in single quotes. Exact.
šiqqûṣêhā 'its detestable things', tôʿăḇôṯêhā 'its abominations'. Exact.

citations: BDB s.v. rûaḥ (sense 'disposition, temper' of the human spirit)
Block, 'The Prophet of the Spirit: The Use of rwḥ in the Book of Ezekiel', JETS 32 (1989)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: wənāṯattî lāhem lēḇ ʾeḥāḏ wərûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ ʾettēn bəqirbəḵem; MT 'one heart' and 'within you' are correctly kept. The question is 'a new ruach': the overlay transliterates every rûaḥ YHWH 'gives', but here rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ is paired with lēḇ as the people's renewed disposition (at 18:31 Israel must 'make yourselves a new heart and a new rûaḥ', and 36:26-27 distinguishes 'a new rûaḥ' from 'my rûaḥ'), which is the overlay's own 'spirit' (human mind) category. Reviewer recommends 'and I will put a new spirit within you', reserving 'ruach' for YHWH's own rûaḥ and the life-breath (36:27; 37:5-6, 14); this is a project-stance call on the scope of the gift clause (founder point C).
Covenant formula; 'their Elohim' without article under elohim-as-translation. Exact.
Difficult wəʾel-lēḇ šiqqûṣêhem ... libbām hōlēḵ given the ASV construal; the wəʾēlleh emendation recorded and not adopted, per the MT baseline.
Cherubim, wheels ləʿummāṯām 'beside them', 'above them from above' (doubled milmāʿlâ kept). Exact.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (Raëlian canon; verified against the FR/EN quotation file)
TBWTT ch. 3 at Ezek 43:2 ('the large ship respectfully called the glory of God')
verdicts.reasoning: English line approved: wayyaʿal kəḇôḏ YHWH ... wayyaʿămōḏ ʿal-hāhār is exact. The reception note overstates the canon: TBWTT ch. 3 quotes 11:23-24 in the run it sums up as 'so many journeys for Ezekiel in one of the creators' flying craft', but it identifies the glory with the creators' large ship explicitly only at 43:2. Proposed note wording: 'quotes 11:23-24 ... among the passages it calls "so many journeys for Ezekiel in one of the creators' flying craft"; the identification of the glory with the creators' large ship is made explicitly at 43:2.' Non-blocking.

ʾēṯ kol-diḇrê YHWH ʾăšer herʾānî 'all the things of YHWH that he had shown me': dāḇār as 'thing' suits 'shown'. Correct.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked every English line, with particular attention to the 16 reception-note sites (2:1, 2:10, 3:3, 3:12, 8:3, 11:1, 11:23, 40:2, 40:3, 42:14, 43:2, 44:2, 44:3, 44:15, 44:18, 44:30). No line carries the canon reading: kāḇôḏ stays 'glory' (11:23; 43:2), the bronze man keeps the Hebrew simile (40:3), qōḏeš stays 'holy' against the canon's 'healthful' (42:14), ʾûlām stays 'porch' against the 'airlock' reading (44:3), and yezaʿ is rendered by its accepted sense (44:18). Each reception note was checked against the TBWTT ch. 3 quotation file and is accurate and labelled, except that 11:23 slightly overstates the canon (verdict revise, notes only). Two features a cold reader might query were judged not to be leakage: 'ruach' (an inferred overlay convention that leaves an acknowledged ambiguity open and replaces the ASV's doctrinal capital) and 'between the land and the skies' at 8:3 (the ratified eretz default and shamayim physical register, identical to GEN-WOH 1:1, with the Hebrew's 'in visions of Elohim' kept). The sacrificial and architectural modernizations ('guilt-offering', 'dash', 'guardroom', 'vestibule', 'altar hearth') follow NRSV/NJPS and the lexica and carry no interpretive content.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 207 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 27 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, sources, overlay, central diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-e2-editor-report.md. After reading it no verdict changed. The report raises nothing on 11:19 (a new ruach), 11:23 (reception-note wording) or 44:24 (Ketiv wording in the line), so those stand. Spot-checks the report requested: NRSV 8:16 'temple', 42:1 'temple yard', 42:3 'in three stories', 43:15-16 'altar hearth', Yadin IEJ 8 (1958), the Mesha line-12 ʾrʾl, and Albright 1942 (ziggurat; arallû) are consistent with the reviewer's knowledge; the '43:3 six manuscripts' count and the exact LXX figure at 40:14 could not be confirmed independently and should be checked against BHS or worded as 'some manuscripts' / 'a different figure' (non-blocking). The report's Ketiv/Qere count (48 readings in 24 verses) matches the reviewer's independent count of 50 bracketed tokens.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-quotation-marks: Ratify the Kings convention for Ezekiel. The reviewer's own stack simulation confirms all eight chapters balance and the 43:7-17 boundary is defensible. Schedule a punctuation-only pass on ch. 37 (37:4-5, 9, 12-14, 16, 19, 21-28) and a check of chs. 1 and 10 so the book ships with one convention.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-proper-names: Keep English forms in Ezekiel for this wave: a mixed book would be worse than either practice, and the three signed-off chapters already use English. Recommendation for the corpus decision: the Latter Prophets volumes (isaiah-woh, ezekiel-woh, daniel-woh) already share English forms while genesis/exodus/Kings transliterate; record that genre split explicitly in a central convention note rather than converting Ezekiel, unless the founder wants decision A extended corpus-wide, in which case the mechanical pass over all eleven chapters is straightforward.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-ruach: Ratify the overlay rule for agent/transport rûaḥ, 'spirit' for human idioms and 'side' for the compass sense, and support merging it with the Kings ruach entries into one central entry. Before promotion, narrow the 'gift' clause: rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ paired with lēḇ (11:19; later 18:31; 36:26a) is the human disposition and should be 'a new spirit', while YHWH's own rûaḥ and the breath of life (36:27; 37:5-6, 14) stay 'ruach'. Verse flag at EZK-WOH-11:19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-inferred-temple-terms: Ship both as inferred. ʾêlām 'vestibule' (NRSV) and harʾēl/ʾăriʾêl 'altar hearth' (NRSV) are lexically supported, replace ASV renderings without lexical basis ('arches', 'upper altar'), and the disputes (40:30 plurals; the 'mountain of El' vocalization) are recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-sacrificial-vocabulary: Ratify the new central entry as direct. 'guilt-offering' and 'dash' are lexically motivated and match NRSV/NJPS and isaiah-woh; Milgrom's alternatives are correctly recorded but not adopted. Add the glossaryRef to EXO-WOH-20:21 and 1KI-WOH-8:63-64 at the next pass of those books.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-refId-prefix: Agree. Normalize EZK- to EZK-WOH- (and GEN- to GEN-WOH-) in one dedicated mechanical central op with a before/after count, separate from any content diff, and only after the Revelation and Ezekiel E2 diffs are both applied.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּשָּׂ֨א אֹתִ֜י ר֗וּחַ וַתָּבֵ֣א אֹ֠תִי אֶל־שַׁ֨עַר בֵּית־יְהוָ֤ה הַקַּדְמוֹנִי֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ימָה וְהִנֵּה֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ וָאֶרְאֶ֨ה בְתוֹכָ֜ם אֶת־יַאֲזַנְיָ֧ה בֶן־עַזֻּ֛ר וְאֶת־פְּלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־בְּנָיָ֖הוּ שָׂרֵ֖י הָעָֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Then ruach lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the house of YHWH, which faces east; and behold — at the entrance of the gate, twenty-five men; and I saw among them Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, officials of the people.

notes.official:
*wattiśśāʾ ʾōṯî rûaḥ* 'then ruach lifted me up' (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`). *šaʿar bêṯ-YHWH haqqaḏmônî* 'the east gate of the house of YHWH' is where the glory stood at 10:19. The twenty-five men here are usually distinguished from the sun-worshippers of 8:16 by place and office.

*śārê hāʿām* 'officials of the people'. *śar* is an official, commander or chief; the ASV 'princes' would give the same English word as Ezekiel's *nāśîʾ* 'prince' (44:3; 37:25), a different office. The overlay entry `sar-and-nasi-officials-and-prince-ezekiel` keeps the two apart (NRSV 'officials of the people'). Names are in their English forms (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-ezekiel`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes 'The spirit lifted me up, and brought me' as another of Ezekiel's journeys in the creators' craft. The line follows the book's rûaḥ convention.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֵ֣לֶּה הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים הַחֹשְׁבִ֥ים אָ֛וֶן וְהַיֹּעֲצִ֥ים עֲצַת־רָ֖ע בָּעִ֥יר הַזֹּֽאת׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, these are the men who devise iniquity and give evil counsel in this city,

notes.official: *haḥōšəḇîm ʾāwen wəhayyōʿăṣîm ʿăṣaṯ-rāʿ* 'who devise iniquity and give evil counsel': two participles describing the governing class left in Jerusalem after 597.

paragraphs.text: הָאֹ֣מְרִ֔ים לֹ֥א בְקָר֖וֹב בְּנ֣וֹת בָּתִּ֑ים הִ֣יא הַסִּ֔יר וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ הַבָּשָֽׂר׃

i18n.en: who say, 'The building of houses is not near; it is the caldron, and we are the flesh.'

notes.official: *lōʾ ḇəqārôḇ bənôṯ bāttîm* is read as a statement, 'The building of houses is not near', the MT sense followed by the ASV (which supplies '[The time]'). The LXX makes it a question ('Have not the houses been newly built?'), and some moderns follow it. The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *hîʾ hassîr waʾănaḥnû habbāśār* 'it is the caldron, and we are the flesh': the city protects those inside it as a pot protects meat from the fire. Ezekiel turns the saying against them in vv 7-11.

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֖ן הִנָּבֵ֣א עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם הִנָּבֵ֖א בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃

i18n.en: Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of human."

notes.official: *hinnāḇēʾ ... hinnāḇēʾ ben-ʾāḏām* 'prophesy against them; prophesy, son of human': the doubled imperative is the Hebrew's. The speech of 11:2-4 closes here.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּפֹּ֣ל עָלַי֮ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָה֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י אֱמֹר֙ כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה כֵּ֥ן אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַעֲל֥וֹת רֽוּחֲכֶ֖ם אֲנִ֥י יְדַעְתִּֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: Then the ruach of YHWH fell upon me, and he said to me, "Say, 'Thus says YHWH: So you have said, house of Israel; and the things that come up in your spirit, I know them.

notes.official:
*wattippōl ʿālay rûaḥ YHWH* 'then the ruach of YHWH fell upon me' (cf. 'the hand ... fell', 8:1). The construct phrase is rendered 'the ruach of YHWH', as at 37:1 (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`; ASV 'the Spirit of Jehovah'). Later in the verse, *maʿălôṯ rûḥăḵem* 'the things that come up in your spirit' (what rises in their minds) is the people's own spirit, and the entry renders that idiom 'spirit'.

The divine speech opens here ('Say, ...'), and the message the prophet is to deliver runs in single quotes from 'Thus says YHWH' to the end of v 12 (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: הִרְבֵּיתֶ֥ם חַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וּמִלֵּאתֶ֥ם חוּצֹתֶ֖יהָ חָלָֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: You have multiplied your slain in this city and filled its streets with the slain.

notes.official: *hirbêṯem ḥalləlêḵem* 'you have multiplied your slain': the people the leaders have killed in the city, not war casualties. This sets up the reversal of v 7.

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ חַלְלֵיכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שַׂמְתֶּ֣ם בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ הֵ֥מָּה הַבָּשָׂ֖ר וְהִ֣יא הַסִּ֑יר וְאֶתְכֶ֖ם הוֹצִ֥יא מִתּוֹכָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Therefore thus says the Lord YHWH: Your slain whom you have laid in its midst — they are the flesh, and it is the caldron; but you shall be brought out of its midst.

notes.official: *ḥalləlêḵem ... hēmmâ habbāśār wəhîʾ hassîr* 'your slain ... they are the flesh, and it is the caldron': the saying of v 3 is reversed. *wəʾeṯḵem hôṣîʾ mittôḵāh* 'but you shall be brought out of its midst'. The MT points *hôṣîʾ* as a third-person or infinitive form ('he has brought out' / 'to bring out'); many manuscripts and the versions read *ʾôṣîʾ* 'I will bring out', as in v 9. The ASV renders the MT with an impersonal passive, 'ye shall be brought forth', and the line does the same (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: חֶ֖רֶב יְרֵאתֶ֑ם וְחֶ֙רֶב֙ אָבִ֣יא עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

i18n.en: You have feared the sword, and the sword I will bring upon you, declares the Lord YHWH.

notes.official: *nəʾum ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'declares the Lord YHWH' (`adonai-yhwh`): the oracle formula stays inside the quoted message (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִתּוֹכָ֔הּ וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־זָרִ֑ים וְעָשִׂ֛יתִי בָכֶ֖ם שְׁפָטִֽים׃

i18n.en: I will bring you out of its midst and give you into the hand of strangers, and I will execute judgments among you.

notes.official: *bəyaḏ-zārîm* 'into the hand of strangers': *zār* is 'foreign, outsider'. *wəʿāśîṯî ḇāḵem šəp̄āṭîm* 'and I will execute judgments among you'.

paragraphs.text: בַּחֶ֣רֶב תִּפֹּ֔לוּ עַל־גְּב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶשְׁפּ֣וֹט אֶתְכֶ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: By the sword you shall fall; at the border of Israel I will judge you; and you shall know that I am YHWH.

notes.official: *ʿal-gəḇûl yiśrāʾēl ʾešpôṭ ʾeṯḵem* 'at the border of Israel I will judge you'. Commentators connect the verse with the execution of Jerusalem's leaders at Riblah in the land of Hamath (2 Kgs 25:18-21; Jer 52:24-27). *wîḏaʿtem kî-ʾănî YHWH* 'and you shall know that I am YHWH' is Ezekiel's recognition formula.

paragraphs.text: הִ֗יא לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְסִ֔יר וְאַתֶּ֛ם תִּהְי֥וּ בְתוֹכָ֖הּ לְבָשָׂ֑ר אֶל־גְּב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֶתְכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: It shall not be a caldron for you, nor shall you be flesh in its midst; at the border of Israel I will judge you,

paragraphs.text: וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּחֻקַּי֙ לֹ֣א הֲלַכְתֶּ֔ם וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י לֹ֣א עֲשִׂיתֶ֑ם וּֽכְמִשְׁפְּטֵ֧י הַגּוֹיִ֛ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר סְבִיבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם עֲשִׂיתֶֽם׃

i18n.en: and you shall know that I am YHWH, in whose statutes you have not walked and whose ordinances you have not done, but according to the ordinances of the nations that are around you you have done.'"

notes.official: *ʾăšer bəḥuqqay lōʾ hălaḵtem ûmišpāṭay lōʾ ʿăśîṯem* 'in whose statutes you have not walked and whose ordinances you have not done': *ḥuqqîm* 'statutes' and *mišpāṭîm* 'ordinances' as in the ASV. *wəḵəmišpəṭê haggôyim* 'but according to the ordinances of the nations': at 5:7 the charge is that they have not even kept those. The quoted message (11:5-12) and the divine speech close here.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהִנָּ֣בְאִ֔י וּפְלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־בְּנָיָ֖ה מֵ֑ת וָאֶפֹּ֨ל עַל־פָּנַ֜י וָאֶזְעַ֣ק קוֹל־גָּד֗וֹל וָאֹמַר֙ אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כָּלָה֙ אַתָּ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as I was prophesying, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. And I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice and said, "Ah, Lord YHWH! Are you making a full end of the remnant of Israel?"

notes.official: *ûp̄əlaṭyāhû ḇen-bənāyâ mēṯ* 'that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died'. The name means 'YHWH rescues', and the prophet's cry speaks of the 'remnant' (*šəʾērîṯ*), which commentators read against the name's echo of *pəlēṭâ* 'escaped remnant' (Zimmerli; Greenberg). *ʾăhāh ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'Ah, Lord YHWH!' (cf. 4:14; 9:8). *hăḵālâ ʾattâ ʿōśeh* 'are you making a full end'.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: The word of YHWH came to me, saying:

notes.official: *wayhî ḏəḇar-YHWH ʾēlay lēʾmōr* 'The word of YHWH came to me, saying' (`davar-yhwh-prophetic-formula`); the formula ends with a colon and the speech opens in v 15.

paragraphs.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם אַחֶ֤יךָ אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י גְאֻלָּתֶ֔ךָ וְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כֻּלֹּ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ אָמְר֨וּ לָהֶ֜ם יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם רַֽחֲקוּ֙ מֵעַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: "Son of human, your brothers, your brothers, the men of your kindred, and the whole house of Israel, all of it — they are those to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Keep far from YHWH; to us this land has been given as a possession.'

notes.official:
*ʾaḥêḵā ʾaḥêḵā ʾanšê ḡəʾullāṯeḵā* 'your brothers, your brothers, the men of your kindred'. *gəʾullâ* is the right and duty of redemption held by the next of kin (Lev 25:24-34; Ruth 4:6), so 'the men of your redemption-right', that is, your kin (ASV 'kindred'). The LXX reads *gālûṯeḵā* 'your exile' ('your fellow exiles'), and NRSV follows it. The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

*raḥăqû mēʿal YHWH* is pointed as an imperative, 'Keep far from YHWH' (ASV 'Get you far'). Unpointed, it could be a perfect ('they are far from YHWH'). *lānû hîʾ nittənâ hāʾāreṣ ləmôrāšâ* 'to us this land has been given as a possession': *môrāšâ* is an Ezekiel term (25:4, 10; 33:24; 36:2-5) (`eretz`).

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֣ן אֱמֹ֗ר כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ כִּ֤י הִרְחַקְתִּים֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְכִ֥י הֲפִֽיצוֹתִ֖ים בָּאֲרָצ֑וֹת וָאֱהִ֤י לָהֶם֙ לְמִקְדָּ֣שׁ מְעַ֔ט בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Therefore say, 'Thus says the Lord YHWH: Though I have removed them far off among the nations, and though I have scattered them among the countries, yet I have been to them a sanctuary for a little while in the countries where they have gone.'

notes.official: *wāʾĕhî lāhem ləmiqdāš məʿaṭ* 'yet I have been to them a sanctuary for a little while'. *wāʾĕhî* is a past narrative form (waw-consecutive with the short imperfect of *hāyâ*), so 'I have been', as in NRSV; the ASV has a future ('yet will I be'). *məʿaṭ* can mean 'for a little while' (ASV) or 'in small measure' (NJPS 'a diminished sanctity'). Rabbinic tradition reads *miqdāš məʿaṭ* as 'a small sanctuary' and applies it to the synagogues and houses of study of the diaspora (b. Megillah 29a). The line keeps the ASV sense of *məʿaṭ*.

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֣ן אֱמֹ֗ר כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ וְקִבַּצְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְאָסַפְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִן־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְפֹצוֹתֶ֖ם בָּהֶ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Therefore say, 'Thus says the Lord YHWH: I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.

notes.official: *wənāṯattî lāḵem ʾeṯ-ʾaḏmaṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'and I will give you the land of Israel'. Ezekiel's characteristic phrase uses *ʾăḏāmâ* 'soil, ground' and not *ʾereṣ*, so central `eretz` does not govern it. A second message in single quotes opens here and runs to v 21.

paragraphs.text: וּבָ֖אוּ־שָׁ֑מָּה וְהֵסִ֜ירוּ אֶת־כָּל־שִׁקּוּצֶ֛יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: And they will come there and remove from it all its detestable things and all its abominations.

notes.official: *kol-šiqqûṣêhā wəʾeṯ-kol-tôʿăḇôṯêhā* 'all its detestable things and all its abominations'. *šiqqûṣ* (detestable thing, often an idol; 2 Kgs 23:13) is kept apart from *tôʿēḇâ* 'abomination' (`toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`) and from *šeqeṣ* (8:10).

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֔ד וְר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וַהֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י לֵ֤ב הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ מִבְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר׃

i18n.en: And I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,

notes.official:
*wənāṯattî lāhem lēḇ ʾeḥāḏ* 'and I will give them one heart'. The LXX and some manuscripts read *ʾaḥēr* 'another heart' (cf. 'a new heart', 18:31; 36:26); the MT 'one heart' (cf. Jer 32:39) is kept. *bəqirbəḵem* 'within you' shifts to the second person inside a third-person sentence. Many manuscripts and the versions read 'within them'. The MT is kept for both readings (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

*wərûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ ʾettēn* 'and a new spirit I will put'. Paired with 'one heart', *rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ* is the people's renewed mind or disposition: at 18:31 Israel is told to 'make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit', and 36:26-27 distinguishes 'a new spirit' (v 26) from 'my *rûaḥ*' that YHWH puts within them (v 27). The book's rule therefore gives 'spirit' here, the category of the human disposition, and reserves 'ruach' for the *rûaḥ* that moves the prophet and for YHWH's own *rûaḥ* given (37:5-6, 14) (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`; ASV 'a new spirit'; BDB s.v. *rûaḥ*; Greenberg, AB 22). *lēḇ hāʾeḇen ... lēḇ bāśār* 'the heart of stone ... a heart of flesh'.

paragraphs.text: לְמַ֙עַן֙ בְּחֻקֹּתַ֣י יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֥י יִשְׁמְר֖וּ וְעָשׂ֣וּ אֹתָ֑ם וְהָיוּ־לִ֣י לְעָ֔ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

i18n.en: so that they may walk in my statutes and keep my ordinances and do them; and they shall be my people, and I will be their Elohim.

notes.official: *wəhāyû-lî ləʿām waʾănî ʾehyeh lāhem lēʾlōhîm* 'and they shall be my people, and I will be their Elohim': the covenant formula (Lev 26:12; Jer 31:33; Ezek 14:11; 36:28; 37:23, 27). *ʾĕlōhîm* is rendered under `elohim-as-translation`; with the possessive no article is used.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

i18n.en: But as for those whose heart walks after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will bring their way upon their own heads, declares the Lord YHWH.'"

notes.official: *wəʾel-lēḇ šiqqûṣêhem wəṯôʿăḇôṯêhem libbām hōlēḵ* is difficult syntax, literally 'and to the heart of their detestable things and their abominations their heart walks'. The ASV construal, 'But as for those whose heart walks after the heart of ...', is kept. Some emend the opening *wəʾel-lēḇ* to *wəʾēlleh* ('but these, whose heart ...'), and that is not adopted (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *darkām bərōʾšām nāṯattî* 'I will bring their way upon their own heads'. The message and the speech of 11:15-21 close here.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ הַכְּרוּבִים֙ אֶת־כַּנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וּכְב֧וֹד אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃

i18n.en: Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the Elohim of Israel was above them from above.

notes.official: *wayyiśʾû hakkərûḇîm ʾeṯ-kanp̄êhem wəhāʾôp̄annîm ləʿummāṯām* 'Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, with the wheels beside them' (`cherubim-ezek`), continuing 10:19. *ûḵəḇôḏ ʾĕlōhê-yiśrāʾēl ʿălêhem milmāʿlâ* 'and the glory of the Elohim of Israel was above them from above' (`kavod-yhwh`; `elohei-yisrael`); the doubled 'above' is the Hebrew's.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֙עַל֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל תּ֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ עַל־הָהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִקֶּ֥דֶם לָעִֽיר׃

i18n.en: The glory of YHWH went up from over the midst of the city and stood on the mountain that is east of the city.

notes.official:
*wayyaʿal kəḇôḏ YHWH mēʿal tôḵ hāʿîr* 'The glory of YHWH went up from over the midst of the city' (`kavod-yhwh`; `kavod-yhwh-departure`). This is the last stage of the departure that began at 9:3 and 10:4, 18-19. *ʿal-hāhār ʾăšer miqqeḏem lāʿîr* 'on the mountain that is east of the city', the Mount of Olives (cf. Zech 14:4). At 43:1-5 the glory returns from the east.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes 11:23-24 ('the glory of Yahweh went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain ... the spirit took me up, and brought me into Chaldea') among the passages it sums up as 'so many journeys for Ezekiel in one of the creators' flying craft'; the identification of the glory with the creators' large ship is made explicitly only at 43:2. The line renders *kāḇôḏ* 'glory' under the central entry, which records the phenomenon without encoding a craft reading.

paragraphs.text: וְר֣וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֗תְנִי וַתְּבִיאֵ֤נִי כַשְׂדִּ֙ימָה֙ אֶל־הַגּוֹלָ֔ה בַּמַּרְאֶ֖ה בְּר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֙עַל֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִֽיתִי׃

i18n.en: And ruach lifted me up and brought me to Kasdim, to the exiles, in the vision, by the ruach of Elohim; and the vision that I had seen went up from me.

notes.official:
*wərûaḥ nəśāʾaṯnî wattəḇîʾēnî kaśdîmâ* 'And ruach lifted me up and brought me to Kasdim'. *kaśdîmâ* is 'Kasdim' with the directional ending. The Kasdim form follows central `eretz-kasdim` (ASV 'into Chaldea'; the full phrase 'the land of the Kasdim' is at 1:3).

*bammarʾeh bərûaḥ ʾĕlōhîm* 'in the vision, by the ruach of Elohim'. The construct is rendered like 'visions of Elohim' (`mar'ot-elohim`), without an English article, under the book's rûaḥ convention (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`). Central `ruach-elohim` ('breath of Elohim') is scoped to Gen 1:2, where the context is cosmological. Here the agent carries a prophet, as at 37:1. *wayyaʿal mēʿālay hammarʾeh* 'and the vision ... went up from me': the vision ends. For the canon's quotation of this verse see the reception note at 11:23.

paragraphs.text: וָאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־הַגּוֹלָ֑ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶרְאָֽנִי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And I spoke to the exiles all the things of YHWH that he had shown me.

notes.official: *ʾēṯ kol-diḇrê YHWH* 'all the things of YHWH': *dəḇārîm* is both 'words' and 'things', and what he speaks is what he was shown.
